title: Service Headroom for Solar and EV Loads
description: Students will evaluate (Bloom Level 5, Evaluate) whether a service has capacity for added EV chargers and will justify (Bloom Level 5, Evaluate) a choice among upgrading the service, reducing the number of chargers, or using load management.
creator: The Science of the Built Environment
author: Dan McCreary
subject: The Science of the Built Environment
chapter_title: Electrical Distribution, Lighting, and Design Team Coordination

concepts: EV charging as a continuous load
prerequisites: Three-phase power: VA = 1.732 x V x I

pedagogical.learningObjective: Evaluate whether a service can carry added EV chargers, and justify a choice among upgrading the service, installing fewer chargers, or using load management.
recommendedUsage: Read the stacked bar: each segment is a Riverbend load group in kVA, and the black line is the service capacity. Hover over any segment to see its VA, its current, and how it was calculated.

Choose the service size and voltage, then set the number of EV chargers and the current of each charger. When the total passes the line, the EV segment turns red and the status line tells you the service is overloaded.
Check Use load management to cap the chargers at the headroom. The readout shows the power each vehicle receives and how long a 36 kWh charging session takes.

Read the three option lines under the status message to compare upgrading the service, installing fewer chargers, and managing the load. Move the PV slider to see the lower bar compare solar production with annual use.
activities: Reproduce (5 min): Set 200 A, 208 V, four chargers at 32 A. Confirm the chapter result: 26,624 VA of chargers against about 12,800 VA of headroom, so the service is overloaded.

Compare (10 min): For each of the three options, record what it costs the owner in money, charging speed, or number of vehicles served. Then try 480 V and 400 A to see how the same loads use less of the capacity.
Decide (10 min): Given a scenario with eight chargers at 48 A and a 400 A service, students choose an option and write a three-sentence justification.
assessment: Students state the largest number of 32 A chargers that fit on a 200 A, 208 V service at full power, and show the arithmetic.
Students explain in two sentences why a 30 kW solar array does not let the service be made smaller.
